panels.title: Talos etcd backup age
panels.description: Age of the last successful talos-backup run (CronJob talos-backup in ns talos-backup, daily 03:17 Europe/Berlin, uploads an age-encrypted etcd snapshot to Hetzner Object Storage). Metric verified live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{cronjob="talos-backup"} = 1789607850 (2026-09-17T01:17:30Z), so the age read 108019s = 30.0h — the 2026-09-18 run had not completed, i.e. the cluster's only etcd backup path is a day stale. Thresholds follow that daily schedule: >26h (93600s) = run is late, >30h (108000s) = the same 30h RPO the CNPG rule BackupTooOld enforces.

panels.title: CNPG clusters with a fresh (<30h) backup
panels.description: Count of CNPG clusters whose most recent available barman backup is younger than 30h. Metric verified live (plugin-barman-cloud v0.15.0; rules.yaml documents this family): barman_cloud_cloudnative_pg_io_last_available_backup_timestamp{cluster!=""} returned 6 series across 5 clusters at 2026-09-18T07:17Z, and max by (cluster) collapses immich's two replicas. Observed fresh = 3 (langfuse 6440s, hindsight 16374s, authentik 18383s). Green requires all 5 — adding a cluster must raise the green step, otherwise the panel reports healthy with a cluster unprotected.

panels.title: CNPG clusters stale or never backed up
panels.description: Clusters whose newest available backup is older than the 30h RPO, or which have never produced one. Observed 2 at 2026-09-18T07:17Z: immich-database and paperless-database report timestamp 0, so the age computes to ~1.79e9s (~56.8 years) — the honest 'no backup exists yet' encoding rules.yaml documents. The alert BackupTooOld fires on 3 series for the same condition because it evaluates per series and immich-database reports from two pods; this panel counts clusters (2). Any non-zero value is red.

panels.title: CNPG backup age by cluster
panels.description: Per-cluster age of the most recent available backup, max over replicas (same series as the two stats). Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: langfuse-database 6440s, hindsight-database 16374s, authentik-database 18383s, immich-database and paperless-database ~1.79e9s (timestamp 0 = never backed up). Sort descending so the worst cluster sits on top.

panels.title: Clusters backed up within 30h (trend)
panels.description: Trend of the fresh-backup count above; it must sit at 5. A step down is a cluster that stopped producing backups — the survivability signal an instantaneous number hides.

panels.title: WAL segments archived per cluster (6h increase)
panels.description: cnpg_collector_pg_wal_archive_status{value="done"} is the core CNPG exporter's count of WAL segments successfully archived; its 6h increase proves the barman-cloud WAL stream is actually flowing per cluster. A flat line means PITR coverage is frozen even while the backup-age gauge looks fine. Live 6h increases 2026-09-18T07:17Z: authentik 1800, hindsight 1068, paperless 519, immich 39, langfuse 34.

panels.title: Closest certificate expiry
panels.description: Minimum remaining validity across every cert-manager Certificate — the tightest cert is what breaks TLS first. certmanager_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds verified live (10 series from cert-manager-controller on the :9402 endpoint named tcp-prometheus-servicemonitor). Minimum at 2026-09-18T07:17Z was 7271538s = 84.2 days (buildctl-client / buildkitd-server, Issuer buildkit-ca). Thresholds: 21 days warn, 7 days critical — past that, cert-manager renewals are failing silently.

panels.title: Five soonest-expiring certificates
panels.description: bottomk(5) of remaining validity with the owning namespace and issuer, so an expiring cert maps to its workload without a second query. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: buildctl-client 7271529s, buildkitd-server 7271529s, clickhouse-operator-serving-cert 7440413s, clickhouse-operator-metrics-certs 7440413s, barman-cloud-client 7487011s (~84-87 days each).

panels.title: Nodes Ready
panels.description: kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="true"} == 1 counted per node. Live: 4/4 nodes (talos-3bi-1fl, talos-919-w9u, talos-bno-yij, home-talos-ingress-fsn1) at 2026-09-18T07:17Z. Red the moment one drops, because the redundancy this platform has is exactly one node deep in places.

panels.title: Nodes not Ready
panels.description: Total nodes (kube_node_info) minus the Ready count above — written this way because a filtered count of status="false" is empty when everything is healthy, and an empty panel is indistinguishable from a broken query. Live: 0 at 2026-09-18T07:17Z (4 nodes total, 4 ready).

panels.title: Scrape targets down
panels.description: count(up == 0) across every scrape target vmagent owns. Live: 2 at 2026-09-18T07:17Z — job=zot (172.20.5.166:5000) and job=unpoller (172.20.5.174:9130). This is a real, current monitoring blind spot, not a dashboard artefact: unpoller being down is exactly why no TrueNAS/ZFS pool series exist in VictoriaMetrics (see the storage row note at the bottom of this dashboard).

panels.title: Flux reconcile errors (1h)
panels.description: Sum of controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total{job="flux-system/flux-controllers"} over 1h — the surviving Flux failure signal on this cluster (see the note panel in this row for why the upstream gotk_reconcile_condition 'not-ready' metric is not usable here). 10 controllers export the counter (alert, bucket, gitrepository, helmchart, helmrelease, helmrepository, kustomization, ocirepository, ...); live increase 2026-09-18T07:17Z was 0 for every one.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: count of ALERTS{alertstate="firing"} — vmalert remote-writes its own alert state into VictoriaMetrics, so this is the live rule-evaluation truth, not a configured-rule count. Live: 7 at 2026-09-18T07:17Z (BackupTooOld x3 for immich/paperless never-backed-up clusters, KyvernoPolicyViolations x4 in audit mode). The breakdown by alertname is the next panel.

panels.title: Monitoring stack targets up
panels.description: Sum of up{} over the five self-monitoring jobs, by their live job labels: vmsingle (1), vmalert (1), vmagent (1), vmalertmanager (1) and vlagent (4 — DaemonSet on all four nodes) = 8 observed at 2026-09-18T07:17Z. This is the 'can I even see the cluster' panel: if the scrape/alerting chain dies, every other panel on this dashboard keeps showing its last known value, which is why the sum is pinned green at exactly 8.

panels.title: Down scrape targets
panels.description: Every up == 0 series, with job/instance so it can be chased down. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: job=zot (172.20.5.166:5000, registry metrics endpoint) and job=unpoller (172.20.5.174:9130, ns unpoller). Both have existed long enough to be a standing gap rather than a restart blip — the zot series matters because the registry is the only image source for first-party images, and unpoller is the only producer of TrueNAS pool capacity data.

panels.title: Flux controller reconcile errors (1h increase)
panels.description: Per-controller error increase (controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total, job flux-system/flux-controllers). Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: all 10 controllers (kustomization, helmrelease, helmchart, helmrepository, gitrepository, ocirepository, bucket, alert, ...) read 0 over 1h. This replaces the upstream gotk_reconcile_condition-based 'not ready' panel that cannot work here (see the note panel in this row).

panels.title: Flux-managed resources by kind
panels.description: count by (kind) of gotk_reconcile_duration_seconds_count — proves the reconcile loop is actually running over the whole GitOps graph (a controller stuck with no reconciles would show nothing here). Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: Kustomization 36, HelmRelease 30, HelmChart 30, HelmRepository 22, GitRepository 1 = 119 series. After a git push, the counts move; a count that silently drops means objects were deleted, not reconciled.

panels.title: Flux readiness: why this row has no 'not ready' count

options.content:
The Flux control-plane dashboard vendored as `dashboards/flux.json`, and every upstream `KustomizationNotReady`-style rule, key off `gotk_reconcile_condition{type="Ready",status="False"}`. **That metric does not exist on this cluster any more.** Verified two ways on 2026-09-18:

* the VictoriaMetrics query API returns **no series** for either `gotk_reconcile_condition` or its replacement `gotk_resource_info` (the pod scrape `flux-controllers` has no relabeling that could drop them, and its other `gotk_*` families arrive fine);
* `curl` of kustomize-controller's own `/metrics` (port-forward to pod port 8080) greps to **0 matches** for both names — the deployed controllers (kustomize-controller v1.9.5, helm-controller v1.6.4, source-controller v1.9.5, notification-controller v1.9.4, i.e. Flux 2.9.x) export only `gotk_reconcile_duration_seconds_*` and `gotk_token_*`.

So readiness is read indirectly here instead of invented: reconcile-error counters (this row), managed-resource counts per kind (GitOps graph is live), and the **Firing alerts** stat above, which counts vmalert's own rule output. When a controller version ships a working readiness metric, replace this note with a `count(... == 0)` panel and delete the guesswork.

panels.title: Monitoring stack components (up)
panels.description: The five self-monitoring jobs behind every other panel on this dashboard, by their live job labels. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: `vmsingle-monitoring-victoria-metrics-k8s-stack` 1, `vmalert-monitoring-victoria-metrics-k8s-stack` 1, `vmagent-monitoring-victoria-metrics-k8s-stack` 1, `vmalertmanager-monitoring-victoria-metrics-k8s-stack` 1, `monitoring/vlagent-monitoring-victoria-metrics-k8s-stack` 4 (VictoriaLogs agent DaemonSet on all four nodes). Eight rows of 1 is the healthy state; anything at 0 means the observability chain has a hole and the rest of this dashboard is stale.

panels.title: Alertmanager notifications vs failures (6h increase)
panels.description: Sent (alertmanager_notifications_total) versus failed (alertmanager_notifications_failed_total) per integration. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: **every integration reads 0 on both**, i.e. Alertmanager has never delivered a notification in the retention window even though the receiver is configured (the failure series carry integration="discord" plus the Alertmanager-internal integrations that always exist). That is the gap this dashboard exists to expose: rules fire (see the Firing alerts panel) but nothing leaves the cluster. Once the Phase-1 external delivery + Watchdog dead-man switch land, the sent line must be non-zero — a flat zero on a survivability dashboard means alerts are being lost silently.

panels.title: Firing alerts by name
panels.description: ALERTS{alertstate="firing"} grouped by alertname — vmalert writes its own evaluation results into VictoriaMetrics, so this is live rule state. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: BackupTooOld 3 (immich-database x2 replicas + paperless-database, all with timestamp 0 = never backed up) and KyvernoPolicyViolations 4 (admission audit, still admitted). A name disappearing without the cause being fixed means the rule stopped being evaluated, not that the problem went away.

panels.title: vmalert rule evaluation errors (1h)
panels.description: sum(increase(vmalert_alerting_rules_errors_total[1h])) — a rule that fails to evaluate is an alert that cannot fire, which is worse than a noisy one. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: 0 (series present, so the metric is real; `vmalert_recording_rules_errors_total` does not exist on this vmalert build and was deliberately not used). Pair with the component-up table: vmalert up + 0 errors = alerting is genuinely working.

panels.title: CNPG WAL archive backlog (segments awaiting archive)
panels.description: max by (cluster) of cnpg_collector_pg_wal_archive_status{value="ready"} — WAL segments written but not yet uploaded to object storage. This is the metric the WALArchivingStalled rule alerts on at >20 for 30m. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: 0 for all five clusters (authentik, hindsight, immich, langfuse, paperless), i.e. no archiving stall. Cells turn red at 20 to match the rule rather than at an invented threshold.

panels.title: WAL backlog by cluster (ready segments)
panels.description: The same backlog over time. It should hug zero; a rising staircase is the precursor to the WALArchivingStalled alert and to a PITR gap, and it is visible here before the 30m `for:` window elapses.

panels.title: Max node filesystem used (%)
panels.description: Highest used percentage across the real block devices the nodes expose. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: 80.08% — the /var xfs volume on instance 10.30.0.23:9100 (the other three read 80.08 / 63.89 / 25.56 / 13.23%). Thresholds 85% warn / 95% critical: on Talos /var holds the kubelet state and containerd image store, so filling it evicts pods and stops image pulls before the disk is actually full.

panels.title: Node /var filesystem used (%)
panels.description: Per-node used percentage of the xfs /var volume (device /dev/sda4 on every node), the only writable filesystem node-exporter reports at a useful mountpoint. Live 2026-09-18T07:17Z: 10.30.0.23 = 80.08% and climbing, 10.30.0.22 = 63.89%, 10.30.0.10 = 25.56%, 2.28.31.116 = 13.23%.

panels.title: Storage pressure: why there is no TrueNAS pool panel

options.content:
The plan called for TrueNAS pool capacity/health from the unpoller exporter. **No such series exist in this deployment**, verified live 2026-09-18:

* `{__name__=~"unpoller.*"}` returns nothing, and the exporter target itself is down — `up == 0` for job=unpoller, instance 172.20.5.174:9130 (see the Down scrape targets panel in the Cluster health row);
* `{__name__=~".*zfs.*|.*pool.*"}` matches only unrelated application series (hindsight_db_pool_*, cilium_operator_lbipam_conflicting_pools) — there is no ZFS/pool exporter scraped by this stack.

Rather than ship a panel whose every query is empty, this row uses the node-exporter `/var` series, which is the storage pressure the *cluster* can actually observe. TrueNAS pool capacity stays an unmonitored local failure domain until unpoller is restored — at which point the panel is added from its then-live metric names, never guessed.
